Analysis/Comments: (Discuss positive and negative aspects of each sale as they affect value)
A total of ten sales were evaluated for comparison to the subject. Each sale has components for comparison to the
subject. The sales are considered to have similar location, land classification, topography and/or production as the
subject. Sales #1, #2, and #3 occurred less than 12 months ago. Sales #4, #5, and #6 occurred less than two years ago.
Sales #7, #8, #9 and #10 are older but representative of similar sized ranches in the subject area. It is reported by local
brokers that the appreciation in this area has averaged about 3% annually over the last four years. The appreciation rate
of 3% utilized in this report has been calculated according to the month of sale through the effective month of this
report. All of the sales are considered to be similar ranch properties as the subject.

The sales are all located within a 75 mile radius of the subject property. The properties are situated in Powder River
County (6 sales), Rosebud County (2 sales), Custer County (1 sale) and Big Horn County (1 sale). Five of the sales
are located to the north; one sale is to the west; one sale is to the south, and three sales are located to the east. Please
refer to the Comparable Sales Map. (continued)

Comments: (Typical area rental terms and conditions) Agricultural properties can be leased on a shared basis or cash rent bases with variances depending upon the terms. Straight cash rental lease rates have been utilized herein. The cash rental rates for the various land classification have been estimated based upon market derived research and conversations with local operators. We believe these rates are reasonable and are typical for the area. The subject ranch has a good balance of hayland and pasture land. It is estimated that about 8% of the ranch's total carrying capacity comes from leased lands. Taxes are based upon Powder River County's 2014 tax year records. Management is estimated at 6% of gross income.

**Analysis/Comments:** Seven sales were analyzed for the value based on the Income Approach. These sales indicate a market derived cap rate ranging from 1.02% to 1.62%. Sale D78 exhibits recreational values on the pasture and reflects the highest cap rate herein. Recreational influences can skew this approach to value, and minor changes in cap rates can have a significant affect on value. The remaining six sales represent a melded cap rate of 1.18% which was used herein to estimate the final value of the subject property based on the Income Approach. This resulted in a total land value of $5,132,000. This approach is considered the least reliable approach to value and was given the least consideration in the final analysis of value.

of Values **Analysis of Each Approach and Opinion of Value:** The primary approaches to value that were used in the analysis of value of the subject property were the Cost Approach and the Sales Comparison Approach. The Income Approach was given the lease consideration in valuation. The Cost Approach is based on the premise that the informed purchaser will pay no more for a property than the cost of construction of an equally desirable substitute with equal utility, less applicable depreciation. The land value within the Cost Approach has been estimated by comparison of the ten comparable sales herein, which are considered to provide reliable comparisons in various degrees. The contributory value of the improvements is approximately 10% of the overall value. Construction costs and depreciation of the buildings were derived from Marshall Swift Building Cost Guide. Physical deterioration, functional obsolescence and external obsolescence were established by the appraiser's general knowledge and by limited market support. Correlation The Sales Comparison Approach herein analyzes comparable sales of similar-type properties. These sales require various adjustments as mentioned in the correlation of comparable sales. No paired sales could be selected for adjustments made, yet relationships for adjustments shown are supported to a lesser degree. Discussion The Income Approach is the conversion of economic benefits into value and is based primarily on the property's productive capacity, requiring measurement of the property's income stream. We have placed less emphasis on this approach in determining an estimate of value for the subject property as it has less relevance to value in the current subject market which is seeing influence from recreationalists and hobby ranchers. In summary, based primarily on the Sales Comparison Approach and the Cost Approach, a final value of $5,200,000 has been concluded for the ***REDACTED*** Ranch property as of January 22, 2015.
